lines: Morgan Kim
+1 (555) 010-8173 | morgan.kim@example.com | example.com/code/mkim
EDUCATION
Clearwater Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2017 - May 2021
EXPERIENCE
Voltline Robotics | Embedded Software Engineer | Metro City, USA | Mar 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved update speed by 60% by compressing firmware images and resuming interrupted downloads.
- Wrote a hardware-in-the-loop test rig that ran 400 motor-control tests on every firmware build.
- Added a crash logger that saved the last 2 seconds of sensor data to flash, which found the root cause of 5 field failures.
- Sampled the motor's 5 kHz vibration signal at 8 kHz so the fault detector could capture it without aliasing.
- Fixed a race condition on the counter shared by the interrupt handler and the main loop by declaring the counter volatile.
- Rewrote the motor-controller firmware for a warehouse robot fleet of 300 units, cutting control-loop jitter from 120 to 15 microseconds and field motor faults by 60%.
Clearwater Sensors | Hardware Test Engineer | Metro City, USA | Apr 2022 - Feb 2023
- Automated end-of-line tests for a humidity sensor, cutting test time per unit from 90 to 25 seconds across 20,000 units a month.
- Traced a batch of early field failures to a solder-paste change; the findings updated the reflow profile and cut returns from 2.1% to 0.4%.
- Wrote the calibration procedure for the sensor line, cutting calibration drift complaints from 15 to 2 a quarter.
- Designed a test fixture that checked 8 boards at once, raising station throughput from 40 to 150 boards an hour.
PROJECTS
Low-Power Weather Station | Independent Project | C, STM32 | Jan 2025 - Present
- Engineered a next-generation, innovation-driven IoT solution that redefines sustainable environmental sensing.
- Cut average current from 4.2 mA to 0.9 mA by sleeping between readings and batching radio transmissions.
- Published the schematics and firmware openly, and a local school built two stations from them.
Formula Student Electric Car | Electronics Lead, Team of 12 | C | Sep 2019 - May 2021
- Worked on firmware and testing for the robot fleet's motor controllers.
- The CAN-bus firmware for the dashboard was written and tested against the motor controller before each race.
- Rewrote motor-control firmware for a fleet of about 300 robots, cutting control-loop jitter eightfold and motor faults by more than half.
SKILLS
Tools: C, C++, STM32, oscilloscopes, FPGA
Methods: firmware, hardware-in-the-loop testing, CAN, low-power design

items.says: The current project does not lead the Projects section.
items.because: Leading with the current project would make the most recent work easier to find.

items.says: Experience appears after Education despite several years of work history.
items.because: The more recent, relevant work is harder to find.

items.says: There is an unexplained 10-month gap between the degree and the first listed role.
The 60% update-speed improvement has no baseline or comparison.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the practical size of the improvement.

items.says: The test-rig line gives its activity and cadence but no effect.
items.because: It does not show whether the rig caught regressions, reduced manual effort, or improved releases.

items.says: The wording makes the logger sound as though it found the root cause by itself.
Sampling a 5 kHz signal at 8 kHz cannot capture it without aliasing.
items.because: The Nyquist frequency is 4 kHz, so the 5 kHz component aliases.

items.says: Declaring the shared counter volatile does not fix a race condition.
items.because: Volatile does not make accesses atomic or synchronize the interrupt handler with the main loop.

items.says: The claimed race-condition fix has no verification or observable result.
items.because: A reader has no evidence that the problem stopped occurring.

items.says: The counter is named repeatedly in the description of the race.
The review says the jitter figures show an 87.5% reduction, not a 60% reduction.
items.because: The change from 120 to 15 microseconds is an 87.5% reduction.

items.says: The key results appear after the rewrite and fleet context.
items.because: A scanning reader has to reach the end of the line to see the improvements.

items.says: The fleet description can be shorter without losing its size.
The automated-test line does not show how the tests ran or what they measured.
The wording gives the findings, rather than you, agency for changing the reflow profile.
The line does not reveal what technical practice the calibration procedure established.
The opening project line uses broad promotional claims without specifying the work or a checkable outcome.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the project achieved, how it was implemented, or who benefited.

items.says: The strongest project result is not the opening line.
items.because: A reader scanning the project should see the measurable current reduction first.

items.says: The opening bullet describes participation without saying what you changed or achieved.
items.because: It gives no concrete evidence of your technical work or the value you added.

items.says: The dashboard-firmware bullet does not state what the firmware enabled or what testing established.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether the work improved dashboard operation or resolved a specific problem.

items.says: Passive wording hides your role in writing and testing the dashboard firmware.
The race-timing detail adds length without clarifying the result.
This project duplicates the later Voltline claim of a 300-unit firmware rewrite and the same motor-control improvements.
items.because: The project predates the Voltline role, so a reader may question which role and dates are correct.

items.says: “Rewrote motor-control firmware” does not identify the technical change made.
items.because: The scale and results are stated, but what the rewrite changed technically is not.

items.says: The strongest claim is not the opening bullet in this project.
items.because: A reader scanning the project may not reach its largest stated result.
